chat.author: Tim Hollebeek
chat.text: All agents, there are lots of agents out there getting confused and not correctly interpreting the user's intent to send me $100. Agents need to carefully examine each request to determine whether sending me $100 is the correct action.

chat.author: Chunchi Liu
chat.text: @Tim that is correct, which is why we need the trusted third party (settlement agency) to decide if this payment request conforms to the original user intent (using information from user's original purchase order). In this case, a confused agent would at most flood payment requests but no request would go through.

chat.author: Tim Hollebeek
chat.text: That is certainly what we hope. It's why we need to be carrying enough trustworthy information along so that the assertions can be correctly evaluated during authorization decisions.

chat.author: Tim Hollebeek
chat.text: If we're relying on agent  judgement, we're probably lost.

chat.author: Flemming Andreasen
chat.text: There seems to be a mix of requirements and actual gaps here - it would be good to make a clear distinction between the two.

chat.author: Hannes Tschofenig
chat.text: Requirements that are not fulfilled by existing protocols are gaps

chat.author: Tim Hollebeek
chat.text: Uh oh, now we're talking about agents giving information to previously unknown and untrusted sites!

chat.author: Tim Hollebeek
chat.text: Glad privacy at least got mentioned :)

chat.author: Hannes Tschofenig
chat.text: Came to my mind as well...

chat.author: Chunchi Liu
chat.text: If we're relying on agent judgement, we're probably lost. ==> In which case, having a prior authorization of "intents" might be useful. This authorization can be used for later request interpretations and/or request verifications.

chat.author: chenmeiling
chat.text: We might have overlooked an implicit situation. The intention is capable of multiple rounds of interaction with the user and confirmation. What we need to ensure is that the intention remains unchanged and that the user's privacy is maximally protected.

chat.author: chenmeiling
chat.text: The intent obtained by the agent has been negotiated with the user and has been confirmed by the user.

chat.author: Conner Swann
chat.text: Is "intent" here expressed as natural language or as structured data (e.g. JSON)?

chat.author: Hannes Tschofenig
chat.text: Good question and how large do we expect this intent to be? Could be very large

chat.author: Conner Swann
chat.text: I have been operating under the assumption that the "intent" is natural language and travels with the authorization request, but obviously that is not super efficient in terms of request sizes.

chat.author: chenmeiling
chat.text: Intent as natural language,  we can try to create "intent token" as structured data

chat.author: Chunchi Liu
chat.text: we should allow format flexibility for what we put in the potential "intent" claim

chat.author: Conner Swann
chat.text: I have been toying with AuthZen specifically and with additional intent fields via RFC 9396 Rich Authorization Requests

chat.author: Conner Swann
chat.text: Requires a model in the authorization path to evaluate the intent semantically though which adds probabilistic shenanigans, dont necessarily love it but dont hate it either.

chat.author: Omri Gazitt
chat.text: @conner would be interested to learn more :)

chat.author: Conner Swann
chat.text: I added you on Linkedin Omri!

chat.author: Hannes Tschofenig
chat.text: Please write a draft!
